result:
CORS is enforced by browser, not server. curl ignores it.

Browser sends request cross-origin (page origin ≠ API origin). Server must reply with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` matching page origin. Header missing or wrong: browser blocks JS from reading response. Server often still processed request.

curl has no origin, no same-origin policy. It never checks those headers.

Common extra cause: preflight. Non-simple requests (custom headers like `Authorization`, `Content-Type: application/json`, methods like `PUT`/`DELETE`) trigger an `OPTIONS` request first. Server must answer it with 2xx plus `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, `Access-Control-Allow-Methods`, `Access-Control-Allow-Headers`. curl skips preflight.

Reproduce in curl:

```bash
curl -i -X OPTIONS https://api.example.com/path \
  -H "Origin: https://your-site.com" \
  -H "Access-Control-Request-Method: POST" \
  -H "Access-Control-Request-Headers: content-type, authorization"
```

Check response for the `Access-Control-Allow-*` headers. Missing: fix on server (add CORS headers or middleware), or proxy request through your own origin. Cannot fix from client JS.

With cookies/credentials: server needs `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` and exact origin, not `*`.
